name: Yash Highvoltage Ltd
tagline: Niche transformer-bushing maker with a genuinely corroborated global shortage catalyst and real FY26 growth — but weak cash conversion, ~75x earnings and steady promoter selling temper the case
business_overview: Yash High Voltage manufactures RIP (resin-impregnated-paper, ~83% of value mix) and OIP (oil-impregnated-paper) high-voltage transformer bushings — a small but critical, highly specialized transformer component (5-8% of transformer cost) with only ~12-13 global manufacturers. It listed on BSE SME in Dec 2024 and is building a Rs 153 Cr greenfield facility at Vadodara (part-funded by a Rs 151 Cr June-2026 preferential raise of equity + warrants at Rs 721) to move up to 550kV bushings and localize capacitive-core (RIP/RIS) production currently imported. Trial production is targeted for H1 FY27, commercial RIP output for H2 FY27 (October).
fundamentals_table: Sales +57% (Rs 235 Cr), PAT +75% (Rs 37.3 Cr), order book Rs 400 Cr (+166%)
Borrowings Rs 38 Cr (up from Rs 7 Cr in FY24); D/E still low
fundamentals_narrative: Top-line execution is genuinely strong: FY26 revenue Rs 235.2 Cr (+57% YoY), EBITDA Rs 60.4 Cr (25.7% margin, +75%), PAT Rs 37.3 Cr (+75%), highest-ever 7,272 bushing units sold (5,752 in FY25), order book Rs 400 Cr as of Mar-2026 (up 166% from Rs 150 Cr). Capital efficiency is good (ROE ~24%, ROCE ~29%). Management's FY27 guidance is to invoice Rs 360-400 Cr (i.e. ~55-70% growth) at ~24-25% EBITDA margin while the new factory ramps, with commercial RIP production from H2 FY27. However, the primary-document read surfaces three things the sentiment pass did not weight: (1) cash conversion is weak and deteriorating — operating cash flow was Rs 14 Cr (FY24), Rs 10 Cr (FY25), Rs 9 Cr (FY26) even as PAT tripled, and FY26 free cash flow was roughly -Rs 50 Cr as capex and working capital absorbed cash (WC days ~69, debtor days ~47); (2) valuation has re-rated to ~75x trailing earnings on a ~Rs 2,947 Cr market cap; (3) promoter holding has drifted from 57.94% (Mar-2026) to 54.79% (Aug-2026), a mix of the Rs 151 Cr preferential issue to non-promoters, a post-listing 'acquirer' group selling ~2.27% in the open market, and an earlier small promoter open-market sale — not a collapse, but a persistent bleed. Borrowings have risen from Rs 7 Cr (FY24) to Rs 38 Cr (FY26) to fund the greenfield, still modest against equity.
technical_read: Not independently pulled this pass; 52-week range Rs 247-873 shows a very wide swing typical of a small, recently-listed SME stock.
sentiment_summary: Newer but very well-documented thread (since Dec 2025) built around a specific, credible structural catalyst: multiple independent company concalls (Quality Power/QPOWER Feb 2026, Apar/TARIL, KEC) have flagged a global 'structural shortage' of high-voltage bushings, driven by AI-datacenter power-density demand plus broader grid/transmission capex, with several posters independently corroborating the same bottleneck from different angles (community member Manik_Gupta tracked this across three separate company concalls). phreakv6 — this project's most-trusted user — wrote a dedicated piece on Yash, referenced directly in-thread.
community_signal: The thread contains an unusually high density of cross-verified, concall-sourced evidence for the core thesis (bushing shortage) rather than speculation — three independent company managements (Quality Power, Apar/TARIL, KEC) corroborating the same supply bottleneck from the buyer side is a stronger signal than typical forum chatter.

bull_case: A genuine, multi-source-corroborated global structural shortage of high-voltage bushings (AI-datacenter and grid-capex driven), independently confirmed across three unrelated companies' concalls — not just Yash's own claims
Real FY26 growth (revenue +57%, PAT +75%, units +26%) with an order book up 166% to Rs 400 Cr and explicit FY27 invoicing guidance of Rs 360-400 Cr
Good capital efficiency (~24% ROE, ~29% ROCE) and still-low absolute debt (Rs 38 Cr) despite the greenfield build
Very small market cap with a narrow global competitive set (~12-13 players) and high certification barriers — a genuine picks-and-shovels niche; 550kV / in-house RIP-core capacity due H1-H2 FY27
phreakv6, this project's most heavily-trusted community voice, has held a personally-researched position since 2025
bear_case: Cash conversion is weak and deteriorating — operating cash flow fell from Rs 14 Cr (FY24) to Rs 9 Cr (FY26) while PAT tripled, and FY26 free cash flow was roughly -Rs 50 Cr; profit is not yet turning into cash
Valuation has re-rated to ~75x trailing earnings (~Rs 2,947 Cr market cap) — the growth is largely priced in and a ramp stumble would de-rate sharply
Promoter / acquirer holding has bled from ~58% to ~55% in months (preferential dilution + open-market selling by the acquirer group and management) — not a collapse, but a persistent negative drip

SME-listing scale means thinner disclosure and lower liquidity; execution risk on the new 550kV / in-house capacitive-core line is real and the company still lacks a technical partner for the higher-voltage segment

Larger global players (Hitachi, Trench, GE) are expanding bushing capacity, which could compress the shortage tailwind; a skeptical poster (Rushin_Shah) questioned Yash's ability to win export share against entrenched incumbents
thesis_fit: 10x-in-2-3-years — small market cap plus a genuinely corroborated structural demand catalyst and real growth keep the classification, but ~75x earnings and weak cash conversion make a literal near-term 10x a stretch; treat as a multi-year rather than 2-3-year multibagger case
verdict_headline: The catalyst corroboration and FY26 growth are real, but the deep read exposes weak cash conversion, a ~75x multiple and steady promoter selling — conviction eases from High to Medium-High
verdict_reasoning: The core catalyst (global bushing shortage) remains the strongest part of the thesis — independently corroborated across multiple unrelated companies' concalls, not just Yash's own claims — and FY26 growth (revenue +57%, PAT +75%, order book +166% to Rs 400 Cr) plus FY27 guidance of Rs 360-400 Cr invoicing are genuine, not projected.

But the primary-document pass surfaces three offsets the sentiment pass under-weighted: (1) operating cash flow has fallen (Rs 14 Cr -> Rs 9 Cr FY24-FY26) while PAT tripled, with FY26 free cash flow around -Rs 50 Cr; (2) valuation has re-rated to ~75x trailing earnings; (3) promoter/acquirer holding has slipped from ~58% to ~55% via preferential dilution and open-market selling.

None of these is a red flag — debt is still low (Rs 38 Cr), the selling is not a collapse, and the capex is a deliberate growth investment — but together they remove the basis for the previous 'highest-conviction call in the batch / High' rating.
trusted_conviction_floor_active is not set for this stock, so phreakv6's 'small position' mention adds weight but does not impose a floor.
Conviction High -> Medium-High. Flagged for continued 30-day revisit given no red flag and thesis fit is not 'neither'; the Q1/Q2 FY27 cash-flow trend and the greenfield ramp are the key watch items.
